## About

I am a labor economist and natural storyteller. My work focuses on topics in people analytics, workforce development, and industrial-organizational psychology. I seek to specialize in data on resumes, job postings data, and compensation data.

Before starting my PhD, I was a Senior Associate in KPMG's Economic & Statistical Consulting practice (Labor & Workforce group), where I did projects in statistical modeling, forecasting, and program evaluation for state and federal workforce agencies. Prior to KPMG I worked in public finance roles across the Denver area that included managing stimulus funds, underwriting municipal bonds, and managing budgets for elected officials.

## Research interests

Labor market analysis, forecasting, causal inference, machine learning for workforce policy, pay transparency and compensation, and job postings and resume data.

## Selected work

- **Pay transparency and the gender wage gap** (master's thesis, University of Colorado Denver). Used CPS microdata to show that pay transparency laws contributed to Colorado leading the nation in reducing the gender wage gap. See [Projects](projects.qmd) and [Writing](writing.qmd).
